tier_rationale: A plain single-pole on/off wall switch in Lutron's Diva line — a mechanical paddle switch with no dimming circuit, no radio, and nothing to configure. The manufacturer's own installation documentation describes only a traditional hardwired installation, with no app, account, or wireless feature anywhere in the procedure, and Lutron's FCC grantee code (JPZ) is well populated with wireless switch/dimmer grants while none exists for this model.
the_unplug_test: This is a paddle connected directly to the circuit it switches. There is no chip in it to lose contact with anything, so a dead router changes nothing about how the lights in the room behave. It turns them on and off the same way a switch has since switches were invented.

repairability.notes: Sold as a sealed wallplate module; Lutron does not publish a component-level repair path. Typical failure is a worn contact, addressed by replacing the low-cost unit.

sources.supports: Manufacturer installation guide for the SC-1PS: a hardwired single-pole switch installed in an existing wall box per electrical code, with no app, account, pairing, or wireless step anywhere in the procedure.

Manufacturer product documentation index confirming SC-1PS is a currently-documented Diva single-pole general-purpose switch, distinct from the Diva dimmer models, with installation guide, performance specification, and wiring diagram documents but no app or connectivity documentation.

Lutron's FCC grantee code JPZ lists numerous wireless dimmer/switch grants (e.g. JPZ0111, a Caseta wireless in-wall dimmer), establishing that Lutron reliably files grants for its radio-equipped models. No grant exists for SC-1PS, which is therefore meaningful rather than a search gap.
